cards.title: Respect for Rank
cards.body: Indonesian military and civilians value hierarchy. Address seniors with their rank and last name. Avoid direct disagreement with superiors to maintain harmony.
doThis: Address seniors with their rank and last name.
Show deference to higher ranks in public.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Indirect Communication
cards.body: Indonesians often avoid direct refusal or criticism to save face. Pay attention to subtle hints and tone. If you must refuse, do so politely and indirectly.
doThis: Listen for indirect refusals or criticisms.
Respond politely to maintain harmony.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy
cards.body: Indonesian culture values hierarchy. Show respect to seniors by addressing them formally and following their lead in meals and conversations.
doThis: Address seniors with their rank and title.
Wait for the eldest to start eating first.
avoidThis: Eat or drink before seniors have started.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Refusals
cards.body: Indonesians may avoid direct refusal to maintain harmony. Pay attention to indirect cues and respect their decisions.
doThis: Look for indirect cues like silence or vague responses.
Accept refusals graciously without pressing further.
avoidThis: Assume a yes means agreement without clarification.
Push for a direct answer if they seem hesitant.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesian culture values respect for hierarchy. When addressing superiors or elders, use formal titles like 'ibu' (mother) or 'bapak' (father), abbreviated as 'bu' or 'pak'. Avoid direct disagreement or criticism to maintain harmony and save face.
doThis: Use formal titles when addressing superiors or elders.
Avoid direct disagreement or criticism.
avoidThis: Use first names with superiors or elders.
Publicly criticize or disagree with superiors.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Indonesian Refusal Etiquette
cards.body: Indonesians often avoid direct refusal to save face. They may use polite phrases implying uncertainty or disagreement. Be patient with pauses and indirect responses. Adapt to the local communication style to build rapport and avoid offense.
doThis: Be patient with pauses and indirect responses.
Adapt to the local communication style.

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesian culture values hierarchy. Address seniors with respect using titles like 'ibu' (ma'am) or 'bapak' (sir). Avoid direct disagreement to maintain harmony.
doThis: Use formal titles when addressing seniors
Avoid direct disagreement to maintain harmony

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Save Face in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesians avoid causing embarrassment. Use indirect language for criticism or refusal. Maintain a polite and friendly demeanor in all interactions.
doThis: Use indirect language for criticism
Maintain a polite and friendly demeanor
avoidThis: Raise your voice or show anger

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Meetings
cards.body: Indonesian workplaces are hierarchical. Seniors are addressed formally and given deference. Criticism is given privately to avoid embarrassment. Meetings often start late and involve relationship-building.
doThis: Address seniors with formal titles and last names.
Avoid interrupting seniors during meetings.
Give criticism privately and tactfully.
avoidThis: Use first names with seniors unless invited.
Disagree openly with seniors in public.
Expect meetings to start and end promptly.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Navigate Checkpoints and Refusals
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Security staff may ask questions. Refusals are often indirect. 'Maybe' or 'We'll see' can mean 'no'. Be patient and polite when dealing with security and local nationals.
doThis: Carry proper identification and base access papers.
Be patient and polite with security staff.
Accept indirect refusals graciously.
avoidThis: Argue with security staff about procedures.
Take indirect refusals as personal rejections.
Lose temper at checkpoints or with local nationals.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Addressing Seniors in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesian culture values hierarchy. Use formal titles and last names for superiors. Women have gained ground but still face challenges in leadership roles.
doThis: Use 'Pak' for men and 'Ibu' for women with their last names.
Acknowledge rank and seniority in interactions.
avoidThis: Assuming leadership roles are equally open to women.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Saving Face in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesians value harmony and avoiding confrontation. Criticism should be given privately and tactfully. Women may face additional social pressures.
doThis: Give criticism privately and gently.
Use indirect language to express disagreement.
avoidThis: Assuming gender roles are strictly traditional.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Respecting Islamic Practices
cards.body: Indonesia is predominantly Muslim. Be mindful of religious practices like prayer times and fasting during Ramadan. Avoid scheduling important meetings during prayer times and be considerate of those fasting.
doThis: Learn basic Islamic phrases like 'Assalamu alaikum' (Peace be upon you).
Respect prayer times and give space when someone is praying.
avoidThis: Eat, drink, or smoke in public during Ramadan fasting hours.
Interrupt or disturb someone during their prayers.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Religious Sensitivity in Conversations
cards.body: Avoid discussing sensitive religious topics unless the other person brings it up. Be respectful of all religious beliefs and avoid making comparisons or judgments.
doThis: Listen actively and show respect for others' beliefs.
Ask open-ended questions if they initiate a religious discussion.
avoidThis: Criticize or mock any religious beliefs.
Assume everyone follows the same religious practices.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving: Respect Hierarchy
cards.body: Indonesians value hierarchy. When giving gifts, present to seniors first. Use both hands to show respect. Gifts are usually refused once or twice before acceptance.
doThis: Present gifts to seniors first
Use both hands when giving
Accept initial refusals gracefully
avoidThis: Give gifts to juniors before seniors

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving: Save Face
cards.body: Indonesians avoid direct disagreement to maintain harmony. If refusing a gift, they may use indirect language. Understand that 'maybe' or 'I'll think about it' often means 'no'.
doThis: Accept refusals politely
Use indirect language if refusing
Understand subtle declines

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Indonesia (2025)

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy at Meals
cards.body: Indonesians serve meals based on age and rank. Wait for the eldest or highest-ranking person to start. Use your right hand or utensils. Avoid eating with your left hand.
doThis: Wait for the eldest or highest-ranking person to start eating.
Use your right hand or utensils to eat.
Compliment the food to show appreciation.
avoidThis: Start eating before the eldest or highest-ranking person.

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints Politely
cards.body: Indonesians value politeness and respect. Use formal language with security staff. Avoid arguing or showing frustration. Be patient and cooperative.
doThis: Use polite and formal language with security staff.
Show your identification and necessary documents clearly.
Be patient and cooperative during checks.
avoidThis: Argue or show frustration with security staff.

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Meetings
cards.body: Indonesian workplaces are hierarchical. Show respect to seniors by using formal titles and their last names. Wait for seniors to start conversations and decisions. Avoid direct disagreements; instead, express opinions indirectly.
doThis: Use formal titles and last names for seniors
Wait for seniors to initiate conversations
Express opinions indirectly
avoidThis: Interrupt or disagree directly with seniors

cards.title: Save Face During Criticism
cards.body: Indonesians value harmony and avoiding embarrassment. Deliver criticism privately and gently. Use suggestions instead of direct blame. If you disagree, do so politely and indirectly.
doThis: Deliver criticism privately
Use suggestions instead of blame
Disagree politely and indirectly
avoidThis: Use direct blame or harsh words

cards.title: Addressing Indonesian Superiors
cards.body: Indonesian culture values respect and hierarchy. Use formal titles and avoid direct disagreement with seniors. Maintain polite language to preserve harmony.
doThis: Address superiors as 'ibu' (ma'am) or 'bapak' (sir)
Use polite language and avoid direct disagreement
Show respect through tone and demeanor
avoidThis: Use first names or informal language with superiors
Publicly criticize or disagree with seniors

cards.title: Radio Etiquette in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesian communication style avoids direct criticism and values politeness. Use clear, respectful language on the radio and avoid abrupt refusals.
doThis: Speak clearly and politely on the radio
Avoid abrupt refusals; use polite phrases
Maintain a respectful tone with all personnel
avoidThis: Use slang or informal language on the radio
Give direct, harsh criticism over the radio

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Indonesia
cards.body: Indonesian culture values hierarchy and respect for seniors. Address seniors with their title and name, and use polite language. Avoid direct disagreement or criticism, as it can cause loss of face.
doThis: Address seniors with their title and name
Use polite and respectful language
Acknowledge and respect hierarchy

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints in Indonesia
cards.body: Checkpoints are common in Indonesia. Always carry identification and follow instructions from security staff. Be patient and polite, as rushing or showing frustration can cause tension.
doThis: Carry identification at all times
Follow instructions from security staff
Be patient and polite
